cards.label: Side cover strip
cards.q: What are the two narrow strips on the sides of the Panda base?
cards.a: Trim strips in Franka's official base mesh; Franka doesn't name them. The base link weighs 2.3966 kg.

cards.label: Rear connector housing
cards.q: What are the three connector housings on the back of the Panda base?
cards.a: Connector shells on the rear panel, identified here by position only; Franka's mesh doesn't name them.

cards.label: Rear connector insert
cards.q: What sits inside each rear connector housing?
cards.a: A dark connector insert. Its role is inferred from position; Franka doesn't label it.

cards.label: Base housing
cards.q: Which Panda axis sweeps the arm's azimuth, and what torque class is it?
cards.a: A1, the base axis: 87 N·m class, like A2–A4. The base casting under it carries the mounting flange.

cards.label: Rear socket face
cards.q: What is the small face on the base's rear socket?
cards.a: The front face of a rear-panel socket, identified by position; Franka's mesh gives it no name.

cards.label: Rear socket
cards.q: What is the socket on the Panda base's rear panel for?
cards.a: Franka's mesh doesn't say. It's identified here by position, and no cable assignment comes with the model.

cards.label: Rear port block
cards.q: What is the block at the rear corner of the Panda base?
cards.a: A port block, identified by position only; Franka's mesh doesn't say which port it is.

cards.label: M8 base mounting screw
cards.q: How is the Panda base bolted down?
cards.a: Four M8 screws through Ø9 holes at 30 N·m; screw type and length depend on the mounting surface.

cards.label: Washer Ø8.4 × 16 × 1.6
cards.q: Why does a washer fit under each Panda base screw?
cards.a: Each Ø9 hole sits in a Ø17 counterbore, room for a Ø16 washer; Franka leaves screws and washers to suit the surface.

cards.label: Ø6 alignment pin (on baseplate)
cards.q: How far apart are the Panda base's two pin holes?
cards.a: 134 ± 0.02 mm, both Ø6 H7. The pins sit in your baseplate and locate the base.

cards.label: M5×8 functional-earth screw
cards.q: How is the Panda base earthed?
cards.a: An M5×8 screw, class 8.8, into the base's M5 thread, with a cable of at least 1.5 mm², no longer than 5 m.

cards.label: M5 tooth lock washer
cards.q: Why does the earth screw get a tooth washer?
cards.a: Its teeth bite through the coating so the earth contact stays reliable.

cards.label: Link shell
cards.q: Which moving Panda link is heaviest, and which is lightest?
cards.a: Link 1 at 2.7907 kg; link 7, the flange, at 0.35973 kg (franka_description inertials).

cards.label: Link-side torque sensor flexure
cards.q: Where does the Panda measure joint torque, and in how many axes?
cards.a: Link-side, between gear output and link, in all 7 axes; libfranka reports it as τ_J.

cards.label: Strain gauges
cards.q: How does a torque sensor flexure turn twist into a signal?
cards.a: Strain gauges on its spokes change resistance as it twists; the electronics read that change as torque.

cards.label: Reduction gearbox (type not published)
cards.q: What gear type do Panda joints use?
cards.a: Franka doesn't publish it; its joint patent only places a gearbox behind the motor and the locking device.

cards.label: Motor stator
cards.q: Which Panda joints are 87 N·m class, and which are 12 N·m?
cards.a: A1–A4 are 87 N·m; the wrist axes A5–A7 are 12 N·m (franka_description limits).
cards.root: stator ← Latin stāre, 'to stand': the part that stays still

cards.label: Stator windings
cards.q: How else can a Panda motor's windings brake the arm?
cards.a: Franka's patent short-circuits them, so the spinning motor acts as a generator and resists motion.
cards.root: copper ← Latin cuprum, from aes Cyprium, 'metal of Cyprus'

cards.label: Rotor on drive shaft
cards.q: What does the Panda rotor's drive shaft carry besides the magnets?
cards.a: The star wheel of the joint's locking brake (patent US10357886B2).

cards.label: Braking star (6 prongs)
cards.q: How does a Panda joint lock when power is cut?
cards.a: A spring drives a head bolt between the prongs of a star wheel on the motor shaft, a form-fit lock.

cards.label: Bearing disc
cards.q: What supports the Panda drive shaft and the locking bolt's actuator?
cards.a: A stationary bearing disc fixed to the joint housing.

cards.label: Locking solenoid (magnet actuator)
cards.q: What holds a Panda joint's locking bolt back?
cards.a: A solenoid, powered while unlocked; iFixit shows it held by 4 × M2 screws with a 2-pin plug to the main PCB.

cards.label: Head bolt (bronze locking pin)
cards.q: What does a healthy Panda lock pin do when the joint unlocks?
cards.a: The bronze pin rises and stays up; if it won't stay up, the solenoid is faulty (iFixit).

cards.label: Motor position sensor disc (θ)
cards.q: In libfranka, how does θ differ from q?
cards.a: θ is the motor position; q is the link position after the gear. The gap between them shows the joint flexing.

cards.label: Joint electronics (main PCB)
cards.q: What connects to each Panda joint's main PCB?
cards.a: Motor control and sensing live on it, and the locking solenoid plugs in with a 2-pin connector.

cards.label: PCB components
cards.q: Do the components on the Panda joint PCBs follow Franka's layout?
cards.a: No. Franka doesn't publish its boards, so these are representative.

cards.label: Joint cap (dark)
cards.q: What are the five dark caps on Panda links 3 to 6?
cards.a: Dark caps over the joint ends in Franka's mesh; the name is inferred from colour and size, since Franka doesn't label them.

cards.label: Cover detail
cards.q: What are the 11 small white cover details on links 3 to 6?
cards.a: Pieces of Franka's official mesh that Franka doesn't name; they're labelled here by colour and size only.

cards.label: Pilot status light (red)
cards.q: Where is the Panda's red status face?
cards.a: On the Pilot panel at the wrist, link 6, beside the green one.

cards.label: Pilot status light (green)
cards.q: What sits beside the Pilot's red status face?
cards.a: A green status face; together they mark the Pilot panel on link 6.

cards.label: Pilot interface panel
cards.q: Where is the Panda's Pilot button panel?
cards.a: On the wrist, link 6, identified by position next to the coloured status faces.
cards.root: pilot ← Italian pilota, from Greek pēdon, 'oar blade'

cards.label: Dark trim
cards.q: What is the dark trim piece on Panda link 6?
cards.a: A dark face in Franka's mesh, named here only by its colour and size.

cards.label: Detail
cards.q: What are the two tiny blue details on link 6?
cards.a: Two small blue faces in Franka's mesh that Franka doesn't name; they're labelled by colour and size only.

cards.label: Pilot bezel
cards.q: What frames the Pilot panel on link 6?
cards.a: A dark bezel, identified by its position around the panel.

cards.label: Flange body
cards.q: What standard is the Panda flange, and what is on its face?
cards.a: DIN ISO 9409-1-A50: 4 × M6 on a Ø50 circle, a Ø31.5 centring bore and a Ø6 pin hole, measured in Franka's mesh.
cards.terms: DIN: Deutsches Institut für Normung (German Institute for Standardization) · ISO: International Organization for Standardization

cards.label: Flange cap
cards.q: What is the small cap on the Panda flange body?
cards.a: A small cap on link 7's flange housing; Franka's mesh gives no further name.

cards.label: Pilot-Grip button
cards.q: What are the two buttons on the Pilot-Grip?
cards.a: Guiding and enabling buttons, identified by their position on the grip.

cards.label: Hand connector
cards.q: Where does the Franka Hand's cable plug in?
cards.a: Into the X6 connector on the Pilot-Grip at the flange.

cards.label: Hand connector socket
cards.q: What is the socket beside the hand connector on the flange?
cards.a: The end-effector connector's socket on link 7, the flange.

cards.label: Pilot-Grip housing
cards.q: What does the Pilot-Grip housing carry?
cards.a: The guiding and enabling buttons at the flange, plus the X6 connector the hand plugs into.

cards.label: Hand base cover
cards.q: What is the light-grey part at the base of the Franka Hand?
cards.a: The hand's base cover. The hand link weighs 0.6544 kg in franka_description.

cards.label: Hand housing
cards.q: How big and how heavy is the Franka Hand?
cards.a: 63 × 205 × 127 mm and 730 g (hand manual), with 80 mm of total finger stroke.

cards.label: Hand cable gland
cards.q: Where does the cable leave the Franka Hand?
cards.a: Through a cable gland on the hand body, followed by a strain relief.

cards.label: Hand cable strain relief
cards.q: What protects the hand cable where it leaves the body?
cards.a: A strain relief that keeps bending and pulling loads off the cable's connections.

cards.label: Finger guide cover
cards.q: How far can each Franka finger travel?
cards.a: 40 mm per finger, 80 mm in total; the thin cover over the finger guides shields that travel.

cards.label: M6×12 low-head screw (hand to flange)
cards.q: What fixes the Franka Hand to the flange, and what limit must you respect?
cards.a: Two M6×12 DIN 7984 screws at 5 N·m; never more than 8 mm screw-in depth.
cards.terms: DIN: Deutsches Institut für Normung (German Institute for Standardization)

cards.label: Ø6h8×10 locating pin (optional)
cards.q: What changes if you fit the Franka Hand without its locating pin?
cards.a: The hand's cable side must then face the Pilot-Grip connector side. The pin is Ø6 h8 × 10 in a Ø6 H7 hole.

cards.label: Fingertip pad
cards.q: What tip radius do Franka fingertips have?
cards.a: R4, a 4 mm radius, and the fingertips are exchangeable (Franka Hand manual).

cards.label: Finger
cards.q: What finger length is the Franka Hand designed and tested for?
cards.a: 54 mm. Each finger fixes to its carriage with two M4×12 screws.

cards.label: M4×12 finger screw
cards.q: How is each Franka finger fixed, and how tight?
cards.a: Two M4×12 screws per finger at 2.25 N·m.

cards.label: DELTA PT 40×10 fingertip screw
cards.q: Which screw holds a Franka fingertip, and how tight?
cards.a: One DELTA PT 40×10 thread-forming screw, M4 class, at just 0.3 N·m.
